title: Qwen3.5-9B Q4_K_M — Atomic Chat on a 16 GB Mac
slug_note: 5.63 GB GGUF inside macOS's ~10.7 GB Metal budget — the biggest model that fits the most common Mac in the room.

variation.quant_detail: qwen35-9b-Q4_K_M.gguf (5.63 GB, HF tree), self-quantized from Qwen's original weights with a per-tensor imatrix

engine.config: Atomic Chat app on macOS 13.6+ (Apple Silicon); its llama.cpp backend. Model found by searching AtomicChat/Qwen3.5-9B-GGUF and picking Q4_K_M. Backend/context not stated.

requirements.notes: Estimate: 5.63 GB Q4_K_M file + short-context KV headroom ≈ 6.5 GB, inside the ~10.7 GB default Metal budget of a 16 GB Mac (mac-16gb record). Close other apps; the pool is shared.

steps.text: Install Atomic Chat for Mac from https://atomic.chat/ (macOS 13.6+, Intel and Apple Silicon).
Open the app, search AtomicChat/Qwen3.5-9B-GGUF, pick a quant, hit Use this model.
Start chatting; the app runs the GGUF on its bundled engine.

caveats: No laptop measurement recorded: status untested. The same 5.63 GB Q4_K_M artifact served as written with llama-server on our DGX Spark on 2026-11-16; that box's speeds do not carry over to a 16 GB Mac.
The AtomicChat GGUF repo ships text-only quants — no vision projector, so this lane has no image input.
Atomic Chat has three swappable backends (see the engine record's gotchas); no speed is claimed here, so attribution does not bind.
